::: {.hero}
# Nelson Rolihlahla Mandela
<p class="lead">1918 – 2013</p>
:::

::: {.quote-block}
"It always seems impossible until it's done."
:::

Nelson Mandela was a South African anti-apartheid revolutionary, political
prisoner, and statesman who served as President of South Africa from 1994 to
1999 — the country's first head of state elected in a fully representative
democratic election. Before entering politics, Mandela trained as a lawyer
and became a leading figure in the African National Congress (ANC), where he
helped organize resistance to the apartheid regime's system of institutional
racial segregation.

Convicted of sabotage and other charges in 1964, Mandela spent 27 years in
prison — most of it on Robben Island — before his release in 1990 amid
growing international pressure and negotiations to end apartheid. In 1993 he
and then-President F. W. de Klerk were jointly awarded the Nobel Peace Prize
for their work toward dismantling apartheid and laying the foundations for a
democratic South Africa.

As president, Mandela prioritized national reconciliation over retribution,
famously establishing the Truth and Reconciliation Commission to address the
crimes of the apartheid era. He retired from public life in 1999 but remained
a global advocate for peace, human rights, and social justice until his death
in 2013.
